questions.question: In a J-K flip-flop if the clock input frequency is 20kHz what is the output at Q
questions.currentExplanation:
A single flip-flop can change its output at most once per clock cycle, so the maximum frequency at Q is half the clock frequency. With the JK flip-flop in toggle mode (J = K = 1) and a 20 kHz clock, Q toggles every clock pulse, giving 20/2 = 10 kHz, i.e. a square wave at half the clock frequency.

Why D is correct: One flip-flop divides the 20 kHz clock by two, so Q is a 10 kHz square wave.

Why the others are wrong:
- A: Q is not held LOW; in toggle mode the output alternates between 0 and 1.
- B: Q is not held HIGH either; a constant HIGH would require J = 1, K = 0 (set mode).
- C: 20 kHz at Q would require no division, but one flip-flop must divide by at least two.

questions.question: Which of the following is correct for a gated D-type flip-flop?

options.text: The Q output is either SET or RESET as soon as the input goes HIGH or LOW
The output complement follows the input when enabled
Only one of the inputs can be HIGH at a time
The output toggles if one of the inputs is held HIGH

questions.currentExplanation:
A gated D-type flip-flop passes data only while its enable is HIGH. While the gate is open Q follows D, so a HIGH input sets Q and a LOW input resets Q; once the gate closes the output is frozen regardless of D. The feature that distinguishes the gated type from the plain D flip-flop is precisely this enable qualifier, which is why option B is the only statement that captures it correctly.

Why B is correct: With the enable HIGH the D flip-flop copies the input onto its outputs, which is what the enabled statement describes.

Why the others are wrong:
- A: As soon as is wrong for a gated D flip-flop, because with the gate closed a change on D has no effect on Q.
- C: Mutual exclusion of two HIGH inputs is a property of the S-R latch, not of a D flip-flop.
- D: Toggling when an input is held HIGH is JK behaviour with J = K = 1; a D flip-flop only follows D.
questions.currentReviewReason: Option B is imprecisely worded (the complementary output follows the complement of D, not D), and option A would be correct for an ungated D flip-flop, so the intended answer cannot be pinned down cleanly.
